questions.q: What is the central message of Father Abraham's speech?
options: Wealth comes mainly from luck and good family connections
Industry, frugality and avoiding debt lead to prosperity
Leisure should be the main goal of all honest labor
A skilled trade matters more than diligence or thrift
questions.explain: The speech urges industry and attention to business, then frugality, and warns against debt.

questions.q: In the speech, what stays bright while rust consumes faster than labor wears?
questions.explain: 'Sloth, like Rust, consumes faster than Labor wears; while the used key is always bright.'

questions.q: In the proverb about neglect, what is ultimately lost for want of a horseshoe nail?
questions.explain: For want of a nail the shoe was lost, then the horse, then the rider.

questions.q: Which does the speaker name as the first vice, ahead of lying?
questions.explain: 'The second Vice is Lying, the first is running in Debt.'

questions.q: How does the speaker treat leisure?
options: As time the diligent earn, for doing something useful
As something to avoid entirely, since idle hours breed vice
As the natural reward of inherited wealth and a good name
As the same thing as laziness, with no meaningful difference
questions.explain: He says the diligent man obtains leisure, defined as time for doing something useful, and leisure and laziness are two things.
